concepts.why: The patient presented with fever, abdominal pain, and vomiting, and developed diffuse papules and purpuric retiform patches, with laboratory tests showing hyponatremia, neutropenia, and elevated C-reactive protein, and tissue culture and blood culture showing positive results for Gram-positive cocci.
The patient developed cavitary lesions in the lungs, representing necrotizing pneumonia, with positive tissue culture and blood culture results for Gram-positive cocci.

The patient developed purpuric retiform patches and diffuse papules, with laboratory tests showing hyponatremia, neutropenia, and elevated C-reactive protein, and tissue culture and blood culture showing positive results for Gram-positive cocci.
The patient developed areas of nonenhancement within both kidneys, suspected to represent renal abscesses, with positive urine culture and blood culture results for Gram-positive cocci.

The patient presented with fever, abdominal pain, and vomiting, and developed neutropenia, with laboratory tests showing hyponatremia, elevated C-reactive protein, and positive tissue culture and blood culture results for Gram-positive cocci.
The patient developed multifocal lesions, likely septic emboli, with positive tissue culture and blood culture results for Gram-positive cocci.

rationales.F06: Purpuric retiform patches are characteristic of Purpura fulminans.
rationales.F10: Cavitary lesions in lungs are indicative of necrotizing pneumonia.
rationales.F11: Gram-positive cocci in vessels suggest Staphylococcal infection.
rationales.F12: Positive tissue culture, blood culture, bronchial washings, and fluid from bilateral empyemas confirm the presence of a bacterial infection.
